deep.reconstruction:
The page has two independent strands.

(A) GENERAL GENUS p: determinant quotients as theta quotients (upper third).

Notation. Σ± a_1^1 a_2^2 ... a_p^p is Jacobi's notation for a determinant, written by its diagonal term. I read the superscript as the index of one of the p everywhere-finite differentials (or integrands) φ^1..φ^p, and the subscript as the index of a point. So D_y(P) = det[φ^j(y_1),...,φ^j(y_{p-1}),φ^j(P)] and D_x(P) = det[φ^j(x_1),...,φ^j(x_{p-1}),φ^j(P)]. The varying points are ε_p, ε_{p+1}, ε_{p+2}, ε_{p+3}, with integral values u_p,...,u_{p+3}. The fixed (p-1)-tuples have integral sums Σu_i (for the y-points) and Σv_i (for the x-points). Primes (u'_i, v'_i) denote the p-1 residual points: those completing y_1..y_{p-1} (or x_1..x_{p-1}) to the zeros of a holomorphic differential.

First formula, as written:
D_y(ε_p) D_y(ε_{p+1}) / [D_x(ε_p) D_x(ε_{p+1})] = ϑ(u_p-u_{p+1}-Σu_i) ϑ(u_p-u_{p+1}-Σu'_i) / [the same with v],
with a further crossed and rewritten variant that mixes u and u' in the denominator.

Why it holds (my reconstruction, implicit on the page):
- Riemann's constants are normalised so that ϑ(u(P)-Σ_{1}^{p} u(η_i)) vanishes exactly at the η_i. Then Σu_i + Σu'_i ≡ 0 modulo periods.
- Hence ϑ(w-Σu') = ϑ(w+Σu) = ϑ(-w-Σu), using evenness of ϑ. This is how the second formula's form ϑ(u_p-u_{p+1}-Σu) ϑ(u_{p+1}-u_p-Σu) arises.
- As a function of P = ε_p, the theta quotient R(P,Q) (Q = ε_{p+1}) is single-valued. Under a b-period the factors e^{-2w_μ-a_μμ} and e^{+2w'_μ-a_μμ} combine to e^{-2(w-w')_μ-2a_μμ}, and w-w' = 2(u_p-u_{p+1}) is the same in numerator and denominator, so the factors cancel.
- The double zero at Q cancels between numerator and denominator. R therefore has zeros {y_i}∪{y'_i} and poles {x_i}∪{x'_i}, exactly like D_y(P)/D_x(P).
- So D_y(P)/D_x(P) = C(Q)·R(P,Q). Symmetry of R in P,Q gives D_y(P)D_y(Q)/(D_x(P)D_x(Q)) = k·R(P,Q), with k independent of P and Q.

Second formula. Riemann removes the unknown constant k by taking the analogous quotient for the pair (ε_{p+2}, ε_{p+3}):
[D_y(p)D_y(p+1)/(D_x(p)D_x(p+1))]·[D_x(p+2)D_x(p+3)/(D_y(p+2)D_y(p+3))] = theta expression.
This gives a constant-free, cross-ratio-like identity expressing determinants of differentials through theta functions.

(B) GENUS 3: Riemann's normal form of the plane quartic (rest of page).

Set-up (top right, and repeated on the next page): six linear forms x, y, z, ξ, η, ζ in three homogeneous variables with
- x+y+z+ξ+η+ζ = 0,
- αx+βy+γz+ξ/α+η/β+ζ/γ = 0,
- α'x+β'y+γ'z+ξ/α'+η/β'+ζ/γ' = 0.
The quartic is √(xξ)+√(yη)+√(zζ) = 0, i.e. 2√(xξyη) = zζ-xξ-yη. Its 7 bitangents (an Aronhold set) are x, y, z, ξ, η, ζ and x+y+z = -(ξ+η+ζ).

The line "-2√(...) = ... -(x+y+z)(ξ+η+ζ)" rewrites the squared quartic using s = x+y+z = -(ξ+η+ζ). Only partly legible.

Restriction to the 7th bitangent x+y+z = 0 (hence ξ+η+ζ = 0):
- Subtract γ(x+y+z) + (1/γ)(ξ+η+ζ) from the second equation. This gives (α-γ)x+(β-γ)y+ξ(1/α-1/γ)+η(1/β-1/γ) = 0, and likewise with primes.
- Equivalently (α-γ)(x-ξ/(αγ)) + (β-γ)(y-η/(βγ)) = 0.
- Dividing by β-γ (resp. β'-γ') and subtracting eliminates y. Note the coefficient of η is -1/(βγ).
- With (αβγ) := det[[1,α,α'],[1,β,β'],[1,γ,γ']] = (α-γ)(β'-γ')-(α'-γ')(β-γ), and (1/α 1/β 1/γ) the same determinant with reciprocals, the coefficients become
  βγβ'γ'[(α-γ)/(β-γ)-(α'-γ')/(β'-γ')] = βγβ'γ'(αβγ)/((β-γ)(β'-γ')),
  (β/α)(α-γ)/(β-γ)-(β'/α')(α'-γ')/(β'-γ') = (1/α 1/β 1/γ)/((1/β-1/γ)(1/β'-1/γ')).
- This leads to a quadratic xx·P + ξξ·Q, and to the conclusion that at the contact points of this bitangent ξ/x (probably (ξ/x)², sign unclear) is ∝ (αβγ)/(1/α 1/β 1/γ). Side computations expand (αβγ) into its six terms.

Other items in this strand:
- A variant quartic, √(ξ(ξ+y+z))+√(η(x+η+z))-√(ζ(x+y+ζ)) = 0: another bitangent representation. Not verified.
- Arrays of 3-bit pairs (e.g. 110/101, (000/011)(ξη)): bookkeeping of genus-3 theta characteristics attached to bitangents and pairs of bitangents.
- The forms (1/α)ξ+βy+γz, αx+η/β+γz, etc.

Bottom: the system 1+αλ+α'λ' = α''λ'' (and the same for β, γ). Then (1, λ, λ', -λ'') spans the kernel of the 3×4 matrix with rows (1, α, α', α''). By Cramer, 1 : λ : λ' : -λ'' = |α α' α''| : -|1 α' α''| : |1 α α''| : -|1 α α'|. So |1 α α'|/λ'' = |1 α α''|/λ' = -|1 α' α''|/λ, which Riemann writes with the reciprocal factors partly crossed out. This continues the λ-computations of the previous page, i.e. determining the constants of the Aronhold-system form.
errors: Second (four-pair) formula: the left-hand factor for (p+2,p+3) is written D_x·D_x/(D_y·D_y), i.e. inverted relative to the (p,p+1) factor. The right-hand side has u in the numerator and v in the denominator for both pairs. For consistency (k cancelling) one of the two second factors must be inverted. Probably a slip, or an ambiguity of the reading.
First formula: the denominator was rewritten with mixed u/u' arguments after the v-version was crossed out. As it stands it is not the v-analogue and seems to be an unfinished variant.
Expansion of (αβγ): the correct value is αβ'-α'β-αγ'+α'γ+βγ'-β'γ. The page as transcribed has +αγ'-α'γ, a sign slip (or misreading).
The final Cramer chain omits the minus sign: correctly |1αα'|/λ'' = |1αα''|/λ' = -|1α'α''|/λ. Possibly absorbed in crossed-out parts.
(ξ/x) = (αβγ)/(1/α 1/β 1/γ) can at best be (ξ/x)² = ∓ that ratio, with sign depending on the exact quadratic form. The page leaves the sign ambiguous.

results.what: Ratio of determinants of holomorphic differentials at p-1 fixed points plus a moving point, expressed as a quotient of products ϑ(u_P-u_Q-Σu)ϑ(u_Q-u_P-Σu); the cross-ratio form with four moving points eliminates the constant.
results.modern_name: Theta-function expression of det(ω_i(x_j)) / Fay-type identity θ(∫_Q^P+e)θ(∫_Q^P-e) ∝ E(P,Q)² ω_e(P)ω_e(Q), with e from a degree p-1 divisor
results.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Riemann 1865 (vanishing theorem) and its school (Weber, Noether, Klein); systematically Fay 1973, 'Theta Functions on Riemann Surfaces'

results.what: Plane quartic as √(xξ)+√(yη)+√(zζ)=0 with x+y+z+ξ+η+ζ=0 and the α,β,γ / α',β',γ' relations (Aronhold set of 7 bitangents).
results.modern_name: Riemann's model of the plane quartic from an Aronhold system
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (lectures/fragment 'Zur Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen für den Fall p=3', ed. Weber; Weber 1876)

results.what: Restriction to the bitangent x+y+z=0, elimination, and determinant forms (αβγ), (1/α 1/β 1/γ) of the coefficients; contact-point ratio ξ/x.
results.modern_name: Computation of contact points of a bitangent in Riemann's quartic model

deep.surprise_reason: The genus-3 quartic material is known Riemann (published via Weber). The general-p determinant/theta cross-ratio identity is a clean statement of a relation usually cited in Fay's 1973 form. It follows from Riemann's vanishing theorem and is plausibly part of his unpublished toolkit; notable as an explicit unpublished formula, but not a major priority shift.
